g-class.name: Mercedes-AMG G 63
g-class.detailedDescription: The AMG G 63 keeps the boxy, ladder-frame silhouette the G-Class has carried since 1979 and puts a hand-built 4.0-litre biturbo V8 under the hood. Three locking differentials and a low-range transfer case survive intact, so the same car that runs to 100 km/h in 4.5 seconds still climbs a 100 percent gradient. Inside it is pure S-Class: Nappa leather, twin 12.3-inch displays and Burmester audio.

porsche-911.name: Porsche 911 Turbo S
porsche-911.detailedDescription: The 911 Turbo S is the everyday supercar benchmark: variable-geometry turbochargers, rear-axle steering and active aerodynamics wrapped in a body 45mm wider than a Carrera. Launch control off the PDK gearbox delivers 2.7 seconds to 100 km/h, yet the car idles through traffic without complaint. Carbon-ceramic brakes and PDCC anti-roll control are standard.

ferrari-296.name: Ferrari 296 GTB
ferrari-296.detailedDescription: The 296 GTB is the first Ferrari road car with a V6, and the first to pair one with a plug-in hybrid system. The 120-degree twin-turbo six and rear-mounted electric motor combine for 830 hp sent to the rear wheels alone. Roughly 25 km of silent electric range sits alongside a 330 km/h top speed and a 1470 kg dry weight.
